quote: we were supposed to have a phone call with you, actually, yesterday to show you that solar estimate, but we weren't able to reach you.
stewart_read: The call reveals this is a recycled/prior-touch lead with an existing solar estimate already prepared, yet the rep never confirms what stage the file is in, what bill/usage data is already on file, or what the customer remembers from the missed appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may already know from internal notes that all qualification data is on file and deliberately skips re-asking to save time.
coaching_implication: Manager should confirm whether reps have visibility into prior-touch records before assuming this was efficient; if not, a quick one-line recap ('let's just confirm what you remember from before we schedule') protects against confusion at the specialist call.

quote: So that works. No. Yeah. You are okay.
stewart_read: This line is garbled/cross-talk in the transcript and doesn't reflect a clean verbal exchange — likely overlapping speech during scheduling. Not coachable content but flags the call had rough patches in communication clarity.
coaching_implication: No action needed; flagged only for transcript quality awareness, not rep performance.

quote: the specialist has some calls going on today. So I don't think you would have time today, but we could totally schedule for tomorrow if you have some time.
stewart_read: Rep is negotiating live without a firm anchor of her own availability window before offering slots — leads to a few rounds of back-and-forth (tomorrow evening, lunchtime, Thursday) before landing. Not a failure since it resolves, but shows the rep didn't come in with a pre-checked slot to offer confidently.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may not have access to the specialist's live calendar and is checking in real time, which is a legitimate operational constraint rather than a skill gap.
coaching_implication: If reps regularly lack real-time calendar access, that's a tooling problem worth flagging to Kenny, not a rep skill issue.

quote: Yeah. So Thursday at 01:30, and then it will just be a phone call. So if you could just have, like, access to your email during the call, just that way he can email you over all the info.
stewart_read: Rep gives a partial button-up — day, time, channel, and one logistics requirement (email access) — but skips the one-hour block statement, the no-driving/computer framing, and the explicit 'is that fair?' handshake.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to add the missing button-up elements even on a short reschedule call — they take seconds and materially reduce no-show risk per schema notes on the handshake.

quote: Alrighty. Well, thank you so much, and we will talk to you on Thursday.
stewart_read: Rep closes the call without promising a text confirmation, which the schema calls out as a required button-up element predictive of show-rate.
coaching_implication: Add 'I'll send you a text confirming Thursday at 1:30' as a habitual close-out line, especially valuable here since this customer already no-showed once.
